entries.claim: When additional swings remain after an intermediate left-target visit, review the endpoint candidate before continuing and consider an explicit gripper_change before_command guard during travel. A pending candidate may begin placement/opening even after changing to the next right-target subgoal. Do not approve that opening merely because the target visit is complete; inspect the fresh candidate. Ordinary cross-table approach need not inherit a short contact-review interval.
entries.conditions: SwingXtimes with cube held and more right-left cycles required. At244, after30-control first-left authorization plus10-control settling prefix, old candidate proposed opening at step6; fresh second-right candidate also proposed opening at step3. Both were withheld, so this is predicted-command risk, not an observed drop. A16-control closed lift/short lateral initiation was followed at260 by retained cube and correct VLA travel; necessity or general superiority of that recovery is unproven. Exact executed error onset and a safe timing bound are not established. Existing duration priors do not address this endpoint carryover.

entries.claim: Separate stop-button approach from contact, but do not assume60 controls remain an approach-only interval after placement. Prefer an initial review around30 controls or an explicit gripper-closure guard, then inspect current front/wrist cap-to-fingertip alignment and use at most one16-control prefix near contact or whenever alignment is uncertain. A before-command gripper_change guard can expose the closure transition; it cannot validate alignment, and an expected safe transition should be approved once rather than repeatedly blocked. These are conditional review recommendations, not safe bounds.
entries.conditions: SwingXtimes press-the-button phase after cube placement. This revises the previous60-control approach suggestion:60 were authorized at420 and already included closure, off-center low descent and retreat by480. Sparse420–480, dense445–480 and original468 show a closed-finger lateral-offset precursor at449 (+29), clear low offset by462 (+42), and low miss at468 (+48). Exact onset of harmful contact is unknown; the precursor could still have been corrected. The earlier episode's90-control authorization also exposed off-center contact late. The current episode ended in official failure612 during later correction, with a separate unresolved swing visit, so button misalignment is not proven to be the sole failure cause. Keep ordinary cube travel separate. Existing guards do not observe object-relative lateral alignment.

entries.claim: Do not advance a swing-visit ledger solely because the EE has settled near a target or the pending trajectory looks finished. If cube-to-target alignment or the visit's visible indication remains ambiguous, resolve the current endpoint before selecting the opposite target. This can require better endpoint interpretation rather than shorter ordinary travel budgets; maintain uncertainty rather than assuming a hidden count.
entries.conditions: SwingXtimes target-visit transitions with the cube held. A first-right phase was reviewed after16 controls and again8 controls later, but the cube remained visibly offset near a gray ring at156/164 and the supervisor switched targets anyway. Sparse140–210 and dense150–179 show that unresolved endpoint and subsequent departure; later reviewed endpoints displayed red rings. Official failure occurred during final button descent612. A missed visit is only a hypothesis: no public counter or failure reason establishes it, absence in unsampled frames is not proof, and this does not define a universal red-ring success requirement. Unlike f7b2738... this concerns accepting/counting an ambiguous visit, not unintended gripper opening. No evidence supports reducing all travel budgets.
